cards.text: Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, rests with his fathers and is buried in the City of David, and his son Jehoram reigns in his place. Jehoram's six brothers get silver, gold and whole fortified CITIES in Judah from their dad, while I went home from a bakery bin for 25 cents. But the kingdom itself goes to Jehoram.

cards.question: Six brothers get silver, gold and cities. Why does the kingdom go to Jehoram?

answers.text: He won a battle for it

cards.question: Once Jehoram has established himself over his father's kingdom, he strengthens himself by putting all his ___ to the sword.
Jehoram's brothers are the only ones he puts to the sword.

cards.text: Jehoram is thirty-two when he becomes king, and he reigns in Jerusalem eight years. He walks in the ways of the kings of Israel, just as the house of Ahab, a king of Israel, had done.

cards.question: Jehoram walks just like the house of Ahab. The text gives the reason: he married Ahab's ___.

cards.text: Jehoram does evil in the sight of the LORD. Yet the LORD won't destroy the house of David, since He had promised to maintain a lamp for David and his descendants forever.

cards.question: Jehoram is doing evil, but the LORD won't destroy the house of David. Along with His promise of a lamp, what's the other reason?

cards.text: Then, in Jehoram's days, Edom rebels against the hand of Judah. Edom basically puts in its two weeks' notice, friend. Except there are no two weeks!

cards.question: Edom rebels against the hand of Judah and appoints their own ___.
Jehoram goes after Edom with just a handful of men.

cards.text: Jehoram crosses into Edom with his officers and all his chariots. And then the Edomites surround him and his chariot commanders, like a surprise party where NOBODY is happy to see you.

cards.question: Surrounded by the Edomites, what does Jehoram do?

answers.text: He rises up and attacks by night
He surrenders to Edom's new king
He sends gold to buy peace

cards.text: So to this day, Edom has been in rebellion against Judah, and at the same time, the town of Libnah rebels too. Two at once. That's my oven timer and my smoke alarm going off TOGETHER.

cards.question: Libnah rebels against Jehoram too. What reason does the text give?

cards.text: Oh, Jehoram's not DONE. He builds high places on the hills of Judah, causes the people of Jerusalem to prostitute themselves and leads Judah astray.
Then Jehoram hears from Elijah, a prophet of the LORD. Not face to face, though.

cards.question: Elijah the prophet has a message from the LORD for Jehoram. How does it reach him?
Elijah's letter says Jehoram has NOT walked in the ways of which kings?

answers.text: Jehoshaphat and Asa king of Judah
Ahab and the kings of Israel

cards.question: Elijah's letter says the brothers Jehoram killed were better than him.

cards.text: The letter keeps going: the LORD is about to strike Jehoram's people, his sons, his wives and all his possessions with a serious blow. Friend, I've opened some scary mail, but this makes a FINAL NOTICE envelope look like a birthday card.

cards.question: Day after day, the letter says, Jehoram himself will suffer from a severe ___.

cards.text: Then the LORD stirs up the spirit of some neighbors against Jehoram. And these are NOT the bring-over-a-plate-of-cookies kind of neighbors.

cards.question: Who does the LORD stir up against Jehoram?

cards.text: They invade Judah and carry off everything found in the king's palace, plus his sons and his wives. The whole palace, friend. GONE.

cards.question: Out of all Jehoram's sons, who is the only one left to him?

cards.text: After all this... the LORD afflicts Jehoram with an incurable disease of the bowels. Friend, that's the exact thing Elijah's letter named.

cards.question: Jehoram's disease goes on day after day for two full ___.

cards.text: Finally, his intestines come out because of the disease, and Jehoram dies in severe pain. Friend, I've got nothing funny for that one.

cards.question: When Jehoram dies, his people make a fire in his honor, like they did for his fathers.

cards.text: Jehoram dies to no one's regret and is buried in the City of David. Eight years on the throne, friend, and not ONE person is sorry he's gone.

cards.question: Jehoram is buried in the City of David, but not in the tombs of the ___.

findings.problem: The joke compares the brothers receiving silver, gold and cities with Papa Dorin being bought from a bakery bin for 25 cents. Being given an inheritance and being bought cheap are not the same action. The 25-cent bin is also a callback with no setup in this lesson. Bakers only know about the junk drawer from onboarding.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The callback to being bought from a bakery bin for 25 cents has no setup earlier in this lesson. Onboarding only gives bakers the junk drawer.

rule.text: A callback only works if its setup came earlier in this lesson or conversation.

findings.problem: "The text gives the reason" sounds like a test question about the text, not Papa Dorin pausing mid-story.

rule.text: Ask from inside the passage, the way a storyteller pauses to let the listener lean in. The question comes out of the moment Papa Dorin just set up.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: Edom rebels, the two weeks' notice line, and "Except there are no two weeks!"

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the rebellions, "Two at once.", and the oven timer line.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "What reason does the text give?" sounds like a test question, not Papa Dorin pausing mid-story.

rule.text: Ask from inside the passage, the way a storyteller pauses to let the listener lean in. The question comes out of the moment Papa Dorin just set up.

findings.problem: Verse 15's details about the disease of the bowels, and the bowels coming out, are never told. The baker only learns "severe illness." Stop 2, card 12 then says the bowel disease is "the exact thing Elijah's letter named," which points back to something the baker never saw.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The card calls the Philistines and Arabs "neighbors" of Jehoram. The text says they "lived near the Cushites" and never calls them Judah's neighbors.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: "The whole palace, friend. GONE." stretches the text. Verse 17 says the invaders carried off the possessions found in the palace, not the palace itself. The line reads as a statement of fact, not a joke.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the invasion, "The whole palace, friend.", and "GONE."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
